methods.name: describe_prefab
methods.description:
What a buildable prefab is before it stands anywhere, in its own frame: placement kind, the turns it takes, its cells, render box, ports, visual top and controls side. Read only.
More: tool_info {tool: "describe_prefab"}

help.text: Its own frame is unturned, x right, y up, z forward, origin snapped as the cursor snaps it. Returns prefab_name, prefab_hash, display_name, build_states, runtime_type, placement (grid, face or face_mount), grid_size_m, small_grid, rotation_axes, allowed_rotations [{facing, up, euler}], small_cells, render_box, grid_box, ports [{index, type, role, flow, at, outward}], visual_up, reversible_flow, has_cursor, controls and, for a rocket engine, engine (topic engine).

engine.summary: A rocket engine's load-time thrust and its feed.
engine.text: engine {name, max_thrust_n (its thrust on its own test fuel at full throttle, as the game fills it at load), max_exhaust_velocity_ms, specific_impulse_s, max_fuel_flow_rate (what that test burn drew in a tick), efficiency (25 is 100 %) and efficiency_percent, mass_kg, chamber_volume_l, feed (pumped_gas, pressure_fed_gas, pumped_liquid or pressure_fed_liquid), inputs [{input, role, pipe, pipe_max_kpa}], and the feed's limits: max_moles_per_tick (pumped gas), litres_per_tick (pumped liquid), max_pressure_per_tick_kpa and flow_rate_min_l/max_l (pressure fed)}. rocket_forecast flies a design with real fuel.

prefab.description: Prefab name (StructureWallLight, as find_things and looking_at report them) or prefab hash.

methods.name: dish_aim
methods.description:
Work out the Horizontal and Vertical (logic degrees) that point a satellite dish at a trader contact, from the dish's own model; nothing moves. Read only: write them with write_logic.
More: tool_info {tool: "dish_aim"}

help.text: Poses the dish's model at trial angles, reads where it would point and restores it within one frame. Returns horizontal, vertical and error_deg (under 2 degrees the contact gets the dish's whole Setting), finished, powered, on, can_rotate, current, stale_pose_deg and samples.

turning.summary: How to turn the dish with the answer.
turning.text: Power the dish and turn it on first, then write horizontal and vertical with write_logic. A dish that cannot rotate stores the angles as its target but never turns, and the game ignores a write of the target it already holds: after powering it, write another value first, then the answer.

reply.text: can_rotate is the game's own check that the dish can turn (finished, powered and on). current gives the dish's angles and error as they stand; current.forward trails the model by the last step of a turn on the Small Satellite Dish, up to a few tenths of a degree. stale_pose_deg above 1 means the dish's animation is not running, so the game's own pointing may lag. samples: how many trial poses the search took.

methods.name: feed_paths
methods.description:
Trace how a network feeds its devices from a root device (an APC output, a generator): the pieces and rooms each feed passes through, daisy chains, and devices no run reaches. Read only.
More: tool_info {tool: "feed_paths"}

help.text: Breadth first over the network's links, so each device gets its shortest path; a device is an end, never passed through. Returns root, network_id, root_room_id, devices [{reference_id, prefab_name, display_name, room_id, pieces, rooms, through, fed_through_other_rooms}], daisy_chains, rooms [{room_id, devices, entries, entry_at, multiple_feeds}], multiple_feeds and unreached. Lists devices 15 and unreached 10 by default.

rooms.summary: How pieces and devices are placed in rooms.
rooms.text: A piece is in the room of a 2 m cell it touches (its own cell first); a device in the room of its grid cell, as rooms has it. rooms lists the rooms a feed passes in order; pieces in no room (inside a floor frame, outdoors) are skipped. through: rooms neither the root's nor the device's own.

methods.description:
Find items anywhere: on the ground, in containers and machines, carried by players, and machine stock. Each with quantity, location, holders and distance, nearest first. 10 per page. Read only.
More: tool_info {tool: "find_items"}

help.text: Each item reports quantity (stack size, else 1), location, held_in (holders from its own slot outwards), the outermost holder's position, and distance from the player. Sorted nearest first. item_totals sums them by type.

methods.name: find_spot
methods.description:
Ranked places for a prefab near a point, on one face plane or on a room's walls, each checked with the game's placement cursor and the layout preview; answers place_arguments. Read only.
More: tool_info {tool: "find_spot"}

help.text: near is a point, "player", "crosshair" (default) or {reference_id}; radius_m default 4, max 12. A mounted piece faces out of the plane with its top up (facing overrides); a standing piece stands on a floor. Returns prefab_name, planes, spots best first (limit 5) [{position, orientation, distance_m, penalty, plane, conflicts, place_arguments}], tried, filtered, checked, rejected and reasons.
help.keys: prefab_name, planes, spots [{position, orientation, distance_m, penalty, plane, conflicts, place_arguments}], tried, filtered, checked, rejected, reasons [{reason, count}], view {source, age_s}.

planes.text: plane with side, or looking: true (the face your look ray hits), or room_id: every level face of a room cell toward outside carrying a wall or window, seen from inside; its floor and ceiling only when named with plane (seen from side, else from the room's side). A plane no room cell touches is invalid_argument. around picks the side in a room.

search.text: Every 0.5 m spot in the radius (nearest first, at most 4000) is aimed as the cursor snaps it and filtered on geometry: small cells free of devices, mounted things and chutes, the mesh box clear of others (no_visual_overlap), the require flags. Then up to max_checks (default 40, max 200) are checked with the placement cursor and the layout preview. require {one_section (default true), min_bottom_above_floor_m, ports_reachable (default false), avoid_doors (default true), front_clear_m (default 0), no_visual_overlap (default true)}. reasons lists why spots fell out, most frequent first, up to 8.

plane.description: A face plane, "z=668": an axis and an even metre.

side.description: The side you view the plane from.

looking.description: Search the face your look ray hits.

around.description: A point near the plane, to pick the side in a room.

room_id.description: A room id: search the room's walls (topic planes).

facing.description: Override the facing every spot is tried with.

one_section.description: One wall section, no seam. Default true.

min_bottom_above_floor_m.description: Its bottom at least this high above the floor.

ports_reachable.description: Every port's joining cell free or joining. Default false.

avoid_doors.description: Nothing in a door's keep-out. Default true.

front_clear_m.description: Metres in front kept free. Default 0.

no_visual_overlap.description: Its mesh box clear of others'. Default true.

require.description: Filters a spot must pass (topic search).

limit.description: Spots returned; default 5, max 20.

max_checks.description: Spots checked with the cursor; default 40, max 200.

methods.name: find_things
methods.description:
Find anything by name or filter: portable tanks, crates, structures, devices, items, players, animals. Filters for kind, class, labels, broken state, atmosphere, maker and location. 8 per page, nearest first. Read only.
More: tool_info {tool: "find_things"}

help.text: name_contains matches the shown name (the Labeller name when there is one) and the game's own name under a label, so 'T1' and 'Portable Liquid Tank' both find a tank labelled T1. min and max keep only things standing in a box (a thing in a slot stands where its outermost holder is). find_items is the tool for item quantities and machine stock.
help.keys: things [{made, reference_id, prefab_name, display_name, custom_name, game_name, kind, runtime_type, ...}], count, total, offset, limit, has_more, scanned, local_player {reference_id, display_name, position}.

reply.text: reference_id, prefab_name, display_name, custom_name (the Labeller name), game_name, kind (item; dynamic: a movable thing that is not an item, such as portable tanks, crates, generators, rovers; structure; entity; other), runtime_type, labelable, location (as find_items has it, built for a structure), carried_by, held_in, position, distance_m, is_device, has_atmosphere, is_broken, condition and made. A rocket's part adds rocket_state (OnLaunchMount, Launching, Landing...): its position moves while it flies. A structure adds rotation {facing, up, euler} in the forms place_structure takes (facing and up null off the grid's axes). A paintable thing adds color {index, name, is_default}, as paint reads it; a structure short of its last build state adds build_state {current, last, complete} (describe_device gives what the next state takes).

broken.text: is_broken is the game's own broken state: at maximum damage, a structure in its broken build state, or a burst pipe (whose damage stays 0). condition is broken, damaged, intact, indestructible or none. The game heals a structure it breaks to 0 damage, so it reads 100 % health: is_broken is the signal, not a health number. remove_structure removes one with allow_broken.

made.text: Every item a fabricator, printer or other machine makes is recorded as it is made (on the host, in memory while the game runs; a stack split off a printed one keeps its record). Each thing reports made {maker_id, maker_prefab, maker_name, game_time_s, quantity, split_from} when the log has it; made_by and made_since filter on it.

examples.text: Every portable tank, gas or liquid, whatever its prefab or label: runtime_type DynamicGasCanister. Everything that holds gas: has_atmosphere true. Every label in the world: labelled_only true. Every wrecked structure: broken true, kind structure.

name_contains.description: Part of the shown or the game's name, any case ('T1', 'Nitrogen', 'Liquid Tank').

prefab_contains.description: Part of the prefab name, any case ('DynamicGasCanister', 'Locker', 'StructurePipe').

labelled_only.description: Only things with a Labeller name. Default false.

broken.description: true: only things in the game's broken state; false: only things that are not.

has_atmosphere.description: true: only things atmosphere_contents has something for; false: only things without.

made_by.description: Only items the print log has from this maker: its id, or part of its prefab or shown name ('Autolathe').

made_since.description: Only items made at or after this game time (game_clock game_time_s); negative: within that many seconds back.

min.description: Box corner, [x, y, z] m; with max: only things in the box.

Read the game clock: game_time_s, paused, time_of_day_ratio and days_past. Read only.
More: tool_info {tool: "game_clock"}

help.text: game_time_s counts seconds, stops while paused and starts from 0 at every launch. time_of_day_ratio is the fraction of the local day, 0 to 1. Values that stop changing between reads mean the game is paused, not that a device is stuck.

methods.name: get_ic_source
methods.description:
Read the source in a circuit holder's chip: IC10, or Lua for a StationeersLua chip. Answers source, language, holder and chip. Read only.
More: tool_info {tool: "get_ic_source"}

help.text: Returns source, source_length, language (ic10 or lua), holder, chip, line_number (IC10 only) and, for a Lua chip, lua as get_ic_status gives it. A large source reads best with output_file.

methods.name: get_ic_status
methods.description:
Inspect a circuit holder's chip: current line, registers, stack window, aliases, defines, pins d0 to d5, power and pause state, compile and runtime errors, a Lua chip's log. Read only.
More: tool_info {tool: "get_ic_status"}

holder.summary: housing, operable, pins, and an empty holder.
holder.text: housing.kind is ic_housing, worn_item, computer_board, cartridge or inserted_item. operable says whether the holder runs its chip: a board needs its computer on, powered and fully built; a cartridge its tablet on and powered; a suit or visor a charged battery. pins: each pin with a device or an alias (a pin with neither is left out; name says which pin): the device's reference id, prefab and name, the alias the chip gave it, and reachable (false when the device is not on the housing's data network). A holder with no chip answers only has_chip false, reference_id, gateway_id, holder and pins.

ic10.text: runtime holds the current line, registers, the stack window (stack_start, stack_count), aliases, defines and jump tags. compile_error_line (0-based integer) and compile_error_type say where compiling failed, null while the source compiles; error_line (a string such as "0") and error_type are the last runtime error. A register or stack value that is not finite is a string: "NaN", "Infinity", "-Infinity". runtime is null for a Lua chip.

lua.summary: The lua block of a Lua chip.
lua.text: lua: compiling (read again while true), has_runtime, init_complete (module-level code done, tick(dt) running), running (all of these, no error, not a library), library (a --@module chip other chips require), source_version, last_error {kind compile or runtime, line, message, traceback} or null, log {lines (the last log_lines printed lines), line_count, truncated}, and unavailable when StationeersLua's state cannot be read.

gateway_id.description: Omit or 'world' for every device; a gateway id narrows to its data networks (see gateways).

reference_id.description: The circuit holder: an IC Housing, a worn holder, a Lua board or cartridge, or the chip itself (see chips).

stack_start.description: First stack address to include; default 0.

stack_count.description: Stack values to include; default 64, 0 for none.

log_lines.description: Lua chips: how many of the last printed log lines; default 5, max 200, 0 for none.

include_source.description: true: include the whole source. Default false (source null, source_length still counts it).

methods.name: grid_survey
methods.description:
Read the grid before routing: the 2 m cells of a box or a room, a page at a time (8 cells), with frames, walls, each small cell's occupant and support, the pieces, devices and their ports, and networks. Read only.
More: tool_info {tool: "grid_survey"}

help.text: Pieces and devices are those in the page's cells, so a device spanning pages is listed on each. A page lists at most 40 pieces and 20 devices by default; truncated gives how many, list_limits {"pieces": n, "devices": n} lists more. sections, network_ids, kinds, occupied_only and compact narrow it.

cells.summary: Each cell and its small and support strings.
cells.text: at (its centre, odd metres), room_id, frame {reference_id, prefab_name, build_state, build_states, blocks_air, blocks_gravity}, walls [{face, reference_id, prefab_name, blocks_air}], small and support: 64 characters for its 0.5 m cells at -1, -0.5, 0, +0.5 m on each axis, index x + 4y + 16z. small: '.' empty, 'c' cable, 'p' pipe, 'b' both, 'h' chute, 'd' device, 'o' another small-grid thing, 'r' a rocket's empty cell. support: 'i' inside a frame, 'e' a frame edge or corner, 'f' on a frame's face, 'w' on a wall's plane, 'a' air, 'x' a door's keep-out, 'g' a window.

pieces.text: pieces [{reference_id, kind, prefab_name, at, cell_count and cell_box {min, max, size} (a piece filling more than one small cell; cells lists each with include_piece_cells), ends, network_id, grade; chutes also flow {in, out} and carries}]. devices [{reference_id, prefab_name, display_name, at, rotation {facing, up, euler}, ports [{index, at (the cell a piece joining it stands in), toward (the end that piece needs), type, role, network_id}], umbilical}].

networks.text: networks (include_networks, default true): cable networks with loads and lowest ratings, pipe networks with contents, pressure and gases, chute networks with chute_count, riding items and devices. network_visibility [{network_id, kind, pieces, cells {inside, frame_surface, wall, air}, air_at, refund}]. include_refund adds each piece's refund and each network's total, what remove_* would give back.

rules.text: Frames and walls never block cables or pipes, so runs may pass through frame cells and along wall planes. A device, chute or other small-grid thing blocks both. A pipe blocks a cable only along its own axis, and the other way round. A chute is blocked by any cable, pipe, device, chute or other thing in its cell.

min.description: Box corner, [x, y, z] in metres; with max.

max.description: The other corner; at most 20000 2 m cells.

room_id.description: A room id (rooms), instead of a box.

include_networks.description: Include the networks of the pieces. Default true.

include_refund.description: Add each piece's removal refund and each network's total. Default false.

sections.description: Only these parts: cells, pieces, devices, networks, network_visibility, doors; default all.

methods.name: highlight
methods.description:
Show the player where things are, through walls and terrain, on their screen only: things, a network, or far points, tinted and labelled for a while. Nothing in the world changes.
More: tool_info {tool: "highlight"}

help.text: targets, up to 64, each exactly one of reference_id, reference_ids (up to 1024 things), network_id (every piece of a cable, pipe or chute network, up to 4096) or at (a far point), with color, label and pulse. seconds default 60, max 600; a new call clears the last unless keep; clear only removes. Needs the player's view; distances are from its camera.

drawing.summary: How things and points are drawn.
drawing.text: Things are drawn with their own meshes as the game holds them (every part of a device, a frame at its build state), tinted, with the T-Ray SPU's see-through material, or a built-in one with the depth test off. A label stands at the thing nearest the camera. A point gets a tall beam, wider with distance, and a label with its distance, bearing (degrees clockwise from north, +z; 90 is east, +x) and height difference; out of view, the label and a >> arrow sit at the screen's edge toward it.

reply.text: targets [{index, kind (things, network, point), color, label, pulse, network_id, things (drawn), missing (ids naming nothing), truncated, at, distance_m, bearing_deg, compass, rise_m}], cleared, seconds, renderer (t-ray, built-in, or remote when the player's own game draws), notes, drawn_on (the player whose game drew them) and view {source, age_s}.

refusals.text: no_view and view_stale: no player view (see player/view). network_not_found and no_network: the network target names nothing. no_line_shader and no_xray_material: this game build lacks what drawing needs.

seconds.description: How long to show; default 60, max 600.

keep.description: true: keep what earlier calls drew. Default false.

clear.description: Only remove what is drawn; give nothing else.

resolved_networks.description: The network handles this request resolved, when any: {argument, given, network_id} each (a plain network id that names the network itself is not listed).

methods.name: ignition_risk
methods.description:
Whether the things the player carries would catch fire, by the game's own fire rule: the air around the player and every burnable item with its flashpoint. Lists 12 items. Read only.
More: tool_info {tool: "ignition_risk"}

help.text: Returns player, cell (the air the player stands in: temperature_k, pressure_kpa, energy_j, inflamed, oxygen_mol, in_room), autoignition_min_energy_j (1e7), minimum_ignition_pressure_kpa (1.5) and items. include_prefabs adds every prefab with a flashpoint or autoignition temperature.
help.keys: player {reference_id, display_name, position}, cell {temperature_k, pressure_kpa, energy_j, inflamed, oxygen_mol, ...}, autoignition_min_energy_j, minimum_ignition_pressure_kpa, items [{reference_id, prefab_name, display_name, slot, in_hand, holder, atmosphere, burning, ...}], prefabs [{prefab_name, display_name, flashpoint_k, autoignition_k}].

rule.summary: When a thing lights and keeps burning.
rule.text: A thing lights when the air is burning and hotter than its effective flashpoint, or when the air is hotter than its autoignition and holds more than 10 MJ; once burning it keeps burning while its cell holds over 0.3 mol of oxygen. A hidden slot never burns. Air under 1.5 kPa lights nothing.

items.text: items: every burnable thing carried at any depth, {reference_id, prefab_name, display_name, slot, in_hand, holder, atmosphere (world, internal for a slot that uses its holder's own air such as a suit, or none), burning, hidden, flashpoint_k, flashpoint_effective_k (the flashpoint divided by the air's pressure as a share of one atmosphere, clamped to 1), autoignition_k, ignites_now (the game's own check on that air), health_ratio}.

include_prefabs.description: Also list every prefab's ignition temperatures. Default false.

methods.name: inspect_slots
methods.description:
Inspect a device's slots: occupants, what each slot takes, and every readable slot logic value. Lists 5 slots by default; slot_index reads one. Read only.
More: tool_info {tool: "inspect_slots"}

help.text: Devices only (things with logic): a crate, a lander or a tool answers device_not_found saying it is not a device; container_contents shows the slots of any thing. interactable false marks a hidden slot, which move_item refuses. truncated gives the slot count; list_limits {slots: n} keeps more.
help.keys: gateway_id, reference_id, device {reference_id, prefab_name, prefab_hash, display_name, runtime_type, ...}, slots [{index, underlying_slot_index, display_name, string_key, slot_class, empty, interactable, locked, ...}], count, total_slots.

gateway_id.description: Omit or 'world' for every device; a gateway id narrows to its data networks (see gateways).

reference_id.description: The device's reference id (list_devices).

slot_index.description: One slot index; left out, every slot.

methods.name: item_totals
methods.description:
Total quantity of each item type in the world, split into on_ground, carried, stored and machine_stock, with the holders holding most. Same filters as find_items. 12 types by default. Read only.
More: tool_info {tool: "item_totals"}

help.text: Answers 'how much iron ingot do I have and where'. quantity includes machine stock (a furnace's or centrifuge's load gets its own row with prefab_name null and reagent set); item_count counts items only, machine_stock_entries the machine and reagent pairs. top_holders lists holders_limit holders per type (default 1, 0 leaves it out), each with kind (player, stored or machine_stock) and position.

name_contains.description: Part of the shown name, any case ('Iron Ingot').

location.description: ground, player, stored or machine_stock; default any (see items).

within_id.description: Only items inside this thing at any depth, and its machine stock.

near_player_m.description: Only things whose outermost holder is within this many metres of the player.

limit.description: Item types returned; default 12.

holders_limit.description: Holders per type in top_holders, most first; default 1, 0 for none.

methods.name: label
methods.description:
Rename things as the hand Labeller does: one with reference_id and name, or up to 64 with labels. An empty name gives back the game's name for it.
More: tool_info {tool: "label"}

help.text: Uses the game's own rename: the host's rename syncs to clients and is saved; a multiplayer client sends it to the host. Each result gives written, sent_to_host, previous and current {display_name, custom_name}, read back from the thing.

names.text: As the Labeller writes it: an empty name becomes the game's name for the prefab (stored as that name, not cleared), cut to 200 characters, rich-text tags stripped except on signs and labels.

refusals.text: not_labelable: a class the Labeller cannot rename: pipes, cables, frames, ordinary items, and the pipe-size in-line tanks (StructureInLineTankGas1x2 and the like); the game has no rename for them. Label a sign or device beside one instead. It renames portable tanks and other movable things, every device, the big in-line tanks (StructureInLineTank), hydroponic trays, plants, IC chips and flags; find_things reports labelable. A refusal changes nothing; in the batch form only its own entry fails.

reference_id.description: The thing to rename (find_things, looking_at, list_devices).

name.description: The new name; empty gives back the game's name.

labels.description: Several renames, up to 64, applied in order; instead of reference_id and name.

reference_id.description: The thing to rename.

methods.name: landing_pads
methods.description:
Every trader landing pad, measured by the game's own checks: its largest square, runway threshold, which ships fit, and whether each contact in the sky can land. Read only.
More: tool_info {tool: "landing_pads"}

help.text: The game's pad check moves the landing point of the pad it measures; every check here puts it back, so a landing in progress is never affected. Also count.
help.keys: pads [{reference_id, prefab_name, display_name, position, forward, is_network_center, piece_count, extent, ...}], count.

pad.text: reference_id, prefab_name, display_name, position, forward (+z north), is_network_center (a network with more or fewer than one centre refuses every landing), piece_count, extent {x_tiles, z_tiles} (2 m tiles), largest_square_tiles (the biggest n up to 15 whose n x n pad the game accepts, with the one-tile shifted centre allowed on even sides; a connection piece inside shrinks it), runway_ok (exactly one switched-on runway threshold; null without a network).

ships.text: fits_by_ship: per ship type, {shuttle_type, pad_size_tiles [x, y], runway_tiles (the approach length for planes, not checked against the pad), needs_threshold, fits}. contacts: every trader in the sky, {reference_id, name, shuttle_type, pad_size_tiles, fits, can_land (the game's own landing check: power, error, one centre, storm (planes are exempt), pad size, runway threshold), reason (the game's message, empty when it can land)}.

methods.name: lint_layout
methods.description:
Check a room or a box against the layout rules (lint-rules.json, the save's file over the mod's), from what stands there: replaceability, doors, ports, floating runs, overlaps, solar, oxidiser venting and more. 25 findings. Read only.
More: tool_info {tool: "lint_layout"}

help.text: Returns region, cells, pieces, devices, structures, doors, counts {rule id: n}, findings [{code, level, message, reference_id, other_id, at, subject, rule_id}] problems first, then warnings, then info, total, has_more, rule_source and elapsed_ms. A rule that cannot run on a subject gives a rule_error finding and the rest still run; a rule that does not load is listed in rule_source.errors. lint_rules lists, validates, tests and explains the rules.
help.keys: region, cells, pieces, devices, structures, doors, counts, findings [{code, level, message, reference_id, other_id, at, subject, rule_id}], total, has_more, rule_source {mod_file, save_file, rules, from_save, disabled, ...}, elapsed_ms.

files.summary: The mod's rule file and the save's.
files.text: The audit rules of lint-rules.json: the file the mod ships, with a lint-rules.json in the loaded save's folder (saves\<station>\) taking priority. A rule with the same id takes the mod's place, "enabled": false turns one off, level sets its level, new ids are added. Both files are read again whenever they alter.

rules.text: Problems: not_replaceable (reported first: check_replaceable's rule), solar_outdoor_reinforced, no_oxidiser_vented_outdoors. Warnings: run_in_door_keepout, port_into_doorway, port_cell_foreign_network, floating_run, run_crosses_window, device_visual_overlap, mounted_faces_out_of_room, device_crosses_seam, controls_blocked, cable_grade_matches_network, controller_labels, solar_unshaded, filter_output_capped, fuel_oxidiser_mix_temperature, outdoor_liquid_insulated, deep_miner_column_clear, cable_on_frames. Info: run_along_door, controls_not_on_wall, replaceable_unchecked. lint_rules {action: "list"} gives each rule's description.

room_id.description: A room id (rooms): check its cells.

max.description: The other corner; at most 4000 2 m cells.

limit.description: Findings returned; default 25, max 500.

methods.name: lint_rules
methods.description:
The lint rule set lint_layout audits with and the building tools run on dry runs: list the rules, validate a rule file, list fields and functions, run the examples, explain a finding. Read only.
More: tool_info {tool: "lint_rules"}

help.text: action: list (default), validate, fields, functions, test or explain. Every reply has rule_source {mod_file, save_file, rules, from_save, disabled, errors}. Nothing is written. rule_not_found and subject_not_found name what is missing.
help.keys: action, rule_source {mod_file, save_file, rules, from_save, disabled, ...}, rules [{id, level, level_when, on, source, file, description, select, ...}], types [{name, doc, fields}], sets, functions [{name, signature, doc, form, cached}], tests [{id, passed, examples}], all_passed, explained [{rule, subject, outcome, level, message, error, values}], valid.

format.text: id, level (problem, warning, info; level_when an expression per finding), on (["audit", "dry_run"]), select (a set: pieces, devices, structures, things, ports, cells, networks, rooms, with where <expression>, or pairs(<set>, within: <metres>)), let (named expressions), assert (what each subject must hold), message (with {expression} parts), other, description, examples ({pass, fail}: subjects as their fields; "fn()": value fixes a function's result), enabled.

expressions.text: Typed and checked at load: and, or, not, comparisons, + - * / %, in, matches (glob), matches_regex, ?. and ?? and has(x) for nulls (a value that may be null must be guarded), let x = e in body, if(c, a, b), lists, the collection forms any, all, count, sum, min, max, first, map, filter, flat_map, sort_by and distinct with x => lambdas, member access on the model (thing, port, network, cell, room, slot, world) and library functions (action functions lists them).

refusals.text: rule_not_found: no rule has that id; list names them. subject_not_found: none of the things around the place given is the subject the rule selects; check the rule's select and the place. rule_error: a rule failed on a subject; the finding names the rule, the subject and why, and the other rules still run; fix or disable the rule in the save's file.

actions.text: list: the rules in effect and where each came from; each rule's file and expressions only with full or rule_id. validate: the files in effect, or text (a lint-rules.json's content checked as the save's file); errors give file, rule_id, field, line, column and the character. fields: every object type with its fields. functions: the forms and every library function. test: every rule's examples (or rule_id's) without the world. explain: rule_id on one subject in the world (reference_id, port, other_id or at): outcome skipped, passed, failed or error, message, level, and every value it read.

action.description: list (default), validate, fields, functions, test or explain.

rule_id.description: One rule: in full for list, its examples for test, the rule for explain.

full.description: list: every rule's file and expressions. Default false.

text.description: validate: a lint-rules.json's content, checked as the save's file.

reference_id.description: explain: a thing, network or room id.

port.description: explain: the port index, for a rule over ports.

other_id.description: explain: the other thing of a pair rule.

at.description: explain: a cell, [x, y, z] in metres, for a rule over cells.

List outermost holders with at least one item (lockers, crates, machines, a backpack on the floor) not held by a player: slots used, item totals, position, nearest first. 12 per page. Read only.

List devices: every one in the world, or those on a gateway's data networks; filter by prefab_hash or name_contains. Reference ids are strings. Lists 25 by default. Read only.

List the scopes device tools take as gateway_id: 'world' (every device), then each StationGod Gateway with its status: ready, incomplete or no_data_network. Read only.

methods.name: looking_at
methods.description:
What the player's crosshair is on: the thing the 3 m interaction ray hits and where a longer look ray lands. include adds the player, the button or slot under it, the view, the full hit and the body. Read only.
More: tool_info {tool: "looking_at"}

help.text: Returns target (null for nothing, terrain or past 3 m) and hit {point, distance_m, face, thing}. include adds parts: player, interactable, view, hit (the full hit), body (a structure target's body), or all. A part asked for that is empty (no interactable, no hit) is left out. Hand target.reference_id to any other tool. Needs the player's view.

methods.name: mod_info
methods.description:
The running mod's identity and health: version, pipe name, per-method call counts and times, the game members it reaches, and its cost to the game. Read only.
More: tool_info {tool: "mod_info"}

help.text: pipe_name is the local pipe this game listens on (the server's --pipe), telling which game a server reached when two run on one machine. Lists methods 15 and reflection 10 by default; list_limits keeps more.
help.keys: mod_id, mod_version, assembly_version, informational_version, pipe_name, methods [{method, calls, errors, total_ms, mean_ms, max_ms}], count, reflection [{member, resolved, optional}], missing_count, runtime {uptime_s, world_epoch, request_budget_ms, frames, memory, ...}.

methods.text: methods: every method the mod answers, {method, calls, errors, total_ms, mean_ms (null before the first call), max_ms}, counted in memory after the mod loaded; main-thread time per request; errors are replies with ok false. The pipe reply envelope of the mod carries elapsed_ms, the main-thread time of a request; MCP tool results do not carry it, so use mean_ms and max_ms here.

reflection.summary: The game members the mod reaches.

methods.name: move_gas
methods.description:
Cheat: move gas and liquid between atmospheres or rooms, or delete it, with no pipe, pump or power; it bypasses the game's physics. Ask the user first. dry_run predicts; applied at the next atmospherics tick.
More: tool_info {tool: "move_gas"}

help.text: Each gas leaves with its own share of its heat and arrives with it. Give from and to (or delete: true), gases and amount_mol. Burst, liquid, freezing and boiling checks refuse a move that would harm the receiving side; force skips the burst check only. Host only.
help.keys: transfer_id, status, predicted, joined, from, to, deleted, moved, error, before, amount_mol, ticks, note.

places.summary: What from and to can name.
places.text: A reference id: a thing with an internal atmosphere (canister, portable tank, tank, suit), a pipe (its network), any landing pad piece (the pad network's shared atmosphere, which holds liquids without changing their state), a pipe or landing pad network id, or an atmosphere id from atmosphere_contents. A room: {"room_id": "<id>"} or {"room_of": "<reference id>"}. "planet", from only. A device without its own atmosphere is no_atmosphere; a single world cell is refused (name its room); from and to the same is invalid_argument.

rooms.summary: Moving from and into a room.
rooms.text: A room is every cell of the closed room with air of its own (none at all is no_atmosphere). From a room, gases is required (its breathable air is never emptied by leaving gases out) and each gas is taken from every cell in proportion, in one tick. Into a room, each gas is spread over the cells by volume, settling it at once where the game's mixing would. A room has no burst rating. Into a room, liquid the room's air would lose is would_burst (force moves it anyway): more freezing out than before, or a liquid under its minimum liquid pressure (Water 6.3 kPa) without the heat to boil it all.

planet.summary: Taking gas out of the planet.
planet.text: from "planet" with delete: true and named gases takes those gases out of the planet's air (the mix Terraforming Reloaded reads) and out of its clouds and ice caps. It needs Terraforming Reloaded (terraforming_mod_required; the stock game keeps the planet read-only). Without amount_mol it repeats for 30 ticks to take back what outdoor cells hand back. The reply is queued: read planet for the result. No dry run.

joined.summary: Joined sets the game mixes every tick.
joined.text: joined (default true) follows the joins the game mixes to one composition every tick: a Gas Tank Storage's canisters and its networks; a portables connector's tank and its gas and liquid networks; a connector pipe's tank and its network; a portable tank and the canister in it; a tank or other device with its network; a hydroponics tray with its networks; an open valve's two networks. From a set, each gas comes from every member in proportion; into a set, it goes into the named atmosphere and the game spreads it. to inside from's set is same_joined_set; over 64 members is joined_too_large; joined: false uses the named atmospheres only.

checks.summary: Burst, liquid, freezing and boiling checks.
checks.text: would_burst (predicted and limit kPa in the message; force skips it): each side's settled pressure, members pooled, against every member's rating (a canister's MaxPressure, a portable tank's MaxSetting, each pipe's rating at its cells), each against the pressure outside; things without a rating are not checked. The receiving side is also refused when the move makes it worse: liquid over 2% of a gas pipe network's volume (the game damages it every tick), gas or liquid freezing at the settled temperature, or the pressure once arriving liquids have boiled.

timing.summary: The queue, transfer_id polls and undo.
timing.text: The game changes gas only on its atmospherics thread, so a move is queued and applied at the start of the next atmospherics tick (about half a second; never while paused). The reply predicts from last tick's values: status queued, transfer_id. Call again with only transfer_id: queued, applied (the same shape from live values) or failed (atmosphere_not_found, nothing_to_move, move_failed). The last 64 are kept; up to 64 wait (busy beyond). To undo, move each gas back by amount_mol; energy_j says how far its temperature differs.

refusals.summary: The move_gas errors and what to do.
refusals.text: unknown_gas: use names as atmosphere_contents gives them. atmosphere_not_found, no_atmosphere and refused (a single world cell: name its room): see places. same_joined_set and joined_too_large: see joined. would_burst: see checks; force skips the burst check. nothing_to_move: the source holds none of the gases. busy: 64 moves already wait (is the game paused?). transfer_not_found: an id never issued or older than the last 64. terraforming_mod_required: see planet. not_host: only the host moves gas.

reply.summary: The shape of from, to and moved.
reply.text: {transfer_id, status, predicted, joined, from, to, deleted, moved, error}. from and to: {members [{owner, atmosphere_id, before, after}] (the named one first), total {before, after, after_boiling}, joined_by (the joining devices), room}. before and after: {pressure_kpa, temperature_k, total_mol, gases}. after_boiling is null when nothing boils, a liquid would not all boil, or the atmosphere never changes state. For a room, members is empty and total is the room's air. moved: [{gas, amount_mol, energy_j}].

methods.name: move_item
methods.description:
Move an item, or part of a stack, into a slot with the game's own moves, as an inventory click does: one move, or up to 64 in order. Never through the world, so nothing perishable is left loose.
More: tool_info {tool: "move_item"}

help.text: One move: reference_id, quantity (part of a stack; the rest stays), to_id (the thing holding the slot) and to_slot (an index, or "auto": a matching stack first when merge allows and the whole stack moves, else the first empty slot that takes it). Or moves: up to 64 such objects, each with its own result. A refused move changes nothing for it.
help.keys: index, ok, reference_id, from {id, slot}, to {id, slot}, quantity_moved, merged_into, destination_reference_id, warning, results, count, success_count, error_count.

rules.summary: Stacks, merging, hidden slots, vending machines.
rules.text: A whole item moves as the game moves it (a vending machine keeps its own bookkeeping); part of a stack splits straight into the slot, as the Stacker does; a whole stack can join a matching stack (merge, default true). An item that is not a stack (a water packet, a canister) moves whole and counts as 1. auto skips slots the game's quick moves skip. An item may be moved out of a hidden slot (to rescue one put there by mistake); that also unpacks a package's items one by one and takes items out of a vending machine's store, and nothing goes back into a hidden slot, so such a move cannot be undone.

reply.text: {index, ok, reference_id, from {id, slot} (null for an item in the world), to {id, slot}, quantity_moved, merged_into, destination_reference_id (the stack in the slot after the move), warning}. warning is the game's error when one of its calls failed part way but the slot holds the result: the move is done, so do not repeat it. The batch form adds count, success_count and error_count.

methods.description:

Also count, total_frames, total_outer, paging and local_player. include_inner lists every frame.

exposed.summary: When a face counts as exposed.
exposed.text: The 2 m cell across the face is in no room (rooms are closed spaces of up to 1200 cells, walled by anything that blocks walking), can hold air (no airtight structure in it, not buried in terrain), is open to the frame through the shared face, and, when it holds a one-sheet frame, its air passes the game's storm exposure test (within 1 kPa of the planet's). A sealed space over 1200 cells has no room, so frames facing into it count as outer; a space closed only by one-sheet frames is a room, so its faces do not count though it leaks.

methods.name: paste_blueprint
methods.description:
Cheat: paste a BlueprintMod blueprint at an exact anchor and turn, with no player needed; it skips the game's placement checks. Ask the user first. status reads progress; undo removes the newest paste.
More: tool_info {tool: "paste_blueprint"}

help.text: Needs BlueprintMod; host only. Paste: name (in BlueprintMod's Blueprints folder, or an absolute path), anchor [x, y, z] (where the blueprint's reference point lands: x and z odd whole metres, y even, for the paste to line up with the grid) and rotation (0, 90, 180 or 270, added to its copy angle). Answers {started, file, entries, anchor, rotation, copy_y_angle, expected_duration_s}; the pieces appear over 2 to 30 s, only while the game runs. Run check_replaceable over the pasted pieces.
help.keys: known, active, complete, cancelled, created, failed, skipped, pasted, standing, fingerprint, file, entries, other_active, message, started, anchor, rotation, copy_y_angle, expected_duration_s.

status.text: Progress of the last paste this tool started: {known, active, complete, cancelled, created, failed, skipped, pasted (kept for undo), standing (of those, the ones that exist: a piece the game refused to register counts as created), fingerprint, file, entries, other_active}. Null counts when the paste finished inside the call that started it.

undo.summary: undo: true, and the shared undo stack.
undo.text: BlueprintMod's bpundo: cancels a running paste and removes what it placed, else removes the last completed paste; returns {message}. BlueprintMod keeps one undo stack for every paste in the world, so undo removes the newest paste of anyone: check status and what stands first in a shared world.

notes.summary: Rooms after a paste, and the survival cost.
notes.text: Rooms are not re-evaluated after a paste or undo: run the console command regeneraterooms before rooms. In survival BlueprintMod charges DeanamicMatter from the local player, which a dedicated server lacks: use a creative world there.

refusals.summary: The paste errors and what to do.
refusals.text: paste_refused: BlueprintMod's own message (the same blueprint already pasted there, no local player in survival, not enough DeanamicMatter, or a paste still placing: wait until status is not active). blueprint_failed: a BlueprintMod call failed (a file that is not a blueprint). mod_missing: BlueprintMod has no Blueprints folder yet; pass an absolute path. invalid_argument: a missing file (the message names the path tried), a blueprint with no entries, a rotation not 0, 90, 180 or 270. game_changed: this BlueprintMod lacks a member the tool calls.

overload.text: would_overload: a network after the edit would carry min(potential, required), pooled over what it joins, above its weakest cable (the game burns a cable every power tick). The load is estimated from each device's own state: a battery's charge and free capacity, an APC's or transformer's supply and demand, a solar panel's or generator's rate, a consumer's draw while on and built; only ports in the device's power role count. Where a removal splits a network, each part is checked with the whole old network's numbers.

when_on.text: would_overload_when_on (a warning, never a refusal): safe as the devices stand, but switching on every device on that network that is off (each at the game's ceiling: a station battery's maximum on output and input, an APC's maximum, a power transmitter's 5000 W) would burn a cable at once, such as two full batteries joined while both are off. It follows APCs, transformers and transmitters whose input is on the network, up to 8 deep. The message names the off devices: keep them off, use a higher grade, or keep the networks apart.

gene_sets.summary: Gene sets, units and the top set.
gene_sets.text: A plant item holds one gene set per unit of its stack; seed bags from crates hold one more, unit 0, which planting never reaches. The top set (the last) is the one planting copies, the planted plant's stats read, harvests inherit with mutation, and the network sends. value and stability run from -1 to 1; a positive stability means a smaller random mutation, and it decays toward 0 each generation.

effect.summary: What effect reports for each gene.
effect.text: effect is the stat the gene sets at its value and at both ends of the range. The fifteen scalar genes: {stat, base_<unit>, now_<unit>, at_min_<unit>, at_max_<unit>} with unit s (seconds) or factor (a multiplier). The four band genes: {stat (GrowTemperature or GrowPressure), now (at its value), at_min, at_max}, each {ideal_min_k, min_k} or {ideal_max_k, max_k} (kPa for pressure).

genes.text: GrowthSpeedMultiplier (the save calls it GrowthTimeMultiplier; both are accepted), DarkPerDay, LightPerDay, DroughtTolerance, WaterUsage, LowPressureResistance, LowTemperatureResistance, UndesiredGasTolerance, GasProduction, HighPressureResistance, HighTemperatureResistance, SuffocationTolerance, LowPressureTolerance, LowTemperatureTolerance, HighPressureTolerance, HighTemperatureTolerance, UndesiredGasResistance, LightTolerance, DarknessTolerance.

writing.summary: How a write lands, and per-gene refusals.
writing.text: Each gene gets {index, ok, gene, previous_value, value}, or an error: unknown_gene, or out_of_range (outside -1..1; force writes it anyway); the others are still written. A value that is not a number (null too) refuses the whole call and writes nothing. The edit is saved and inherited by harvested fruit and seeds like a natural gene. Stats read genes live; a write to the top set recomputes the temperature and pressure curves and syncs to clients. A harvest quantity, fixed when the plant first matures, stays as it is.

refusals.summary: Why a read or write is refused.
refusals.text: thing_not_found; not_a_plant (not a plant, seed or produce); no_genes (no gene set yet); unit_out_of_range (the message gives how many sets it has); plant_not_found (plants: no plant has that id); not_host (a multiplayer client cannot write).

gas.summary: gas_to: keep a removed device's gas in a pipe network.
gas.text: The game deletes a device's own gas when it is deconstructed (a tank lets its gas out where it stood); holds_gas refuses that unless allow_contents. gas_to "connected" hands the gas to the first of the device's own pipe networks that the job leaves standing, that carries liquid if the gas holds any, and that stays within its weakest pipe's rating with the gas added; gas_to with a pipe network id, or a pipe on one, names the network. The warning gas_handed_over names the network and the pressure after; gas_to_refused says why no network qualifies, and nothing is removed. The job moves the gas just before the device goes, and its gas check expects the network to hold it.

refusals.text: not_a_structure (items and movable things: use move_item), being_destroyed, indestructible, rocket_moving (a part of a launching or landing rocket), game_refuses (the game's own deconstruct rule; for a fuselage piece also nothing on top and no internals in its cells unless the request removes them), has_mounted (a device mounted on it would be left hanging; remove it in the same request), refund_holder_removed (the refund holder is removed or held by what is removed).

allowed.summary: Refused unless allowed: broken, contents, breach.
allowed.text: broken (the game's broken state; allow_broken removes it as the game does: nothing back, every other guard applies). holds_items and holds_gas (allow_contents: items drop where it stood, a tank lets its gas out, other devices lose it; the last in-line tank or passive vent of a network takes its gas with it, named in moles). contents_would_move (an in-line tank or vent whose removal splits a network holding gas; allow_contents). would_breach (an airtight piece whose removal joins spaces 1 kPa or more apart; allow_breach). Allowed, each becomes a warning: broken_removed, items_dropped, gas_released, contents_deleted, breach. port_left_open warns.

breach.summary: How would_breach follows the game's air rule.
breach.text: The whole request is judged at once. A face stays sealed while anything left on it blocks air, or the structure filling a cell beside it does (a finished frame): a plate on a frame's face never breaches, and two plates back to back breach only when both go. Each opening is reported once, by the first of its pieces in reference_ids.

burst.text: Removing an in-line tank or passive vent that is not the last of its network takes its volume while the gas stays, so the pressure rises; over the weakest pipe left it is would_burst, naming the kPa and the gas to take out first. allow_burst goes ahead where a burst is acceptable (outdoors) and warns will_burst [{network_id, pressure_now_kpa, pressure_after_kpa, rating_kpa, pipes, where, holds_mol, released_mol, gases}]: the pipes expected to burst (only the weakest in a cell holding air), where each leaks, and the gas expected out. The gas check expects that release. allow_burst also lifts it for a request of pipe pieces alone, which remove_pipes refuses outright.

A network the request leaves in one piece keeps its id and all its gas in what is left: every removed member leaves it first, an in-line tank or passive vent removed alone too. Where the request splits a network, each part is a new network with its share of the gas by volume at each split, and would_burst names the one furthest over its weakest pipe. remove_pipes' holds_contents and would_burst for pipe pieces are this model's holds_gas and would_burst.

Walls on its faces are fine and must still be there after (face_structures_changed otherwise). As when the game's last sheet is welded, the cell leaves its room and its gas is divided among its open neighbours; the room check allows for that.

rules.text: Only plain walls and windows are taken or built (a floor grating swaps like a window); shuttered windows and their connectors, other floors, ladder platforms and crew umbilical doors are kept as special_piece, and such a target is invalid_target. The target must be a loaded prefab some kit builds. The new wall must take exactly the old one's face slots (footprint_mismatch otherwise). If the old piece blocks air or gravity, the target must too (would_open); an old leaky piece made airtight is reported as seals. Kept with a reason: already_at_target, special_piece, not_selected, indestructible, broken, being_destroyed.

pressure.text: Each face's pressure difference (the two cells', the planet's where a cell has none) against the face's summed pressure limit with the new wall: at or above it the game would damage the wall until it breaks, so the run is would_overstress. Above the wall's stress mark the piece is flagged stressed (not a refusal). A face beside a frame is shielded: the game never stresses it.

materials.summary: Costs and refunds by the deconstruct rule.
materials.text: Each build state's items with their quantities (tools skipped): the new piece costs states 0 to final, the old one gives back states 0 to its current one, netted per item per piece. The shortfall comes from from_id, the surplus goes back with refund. Tool wear, welder fuel and battery are not charged. not_enough_materials names each missing item.

checks.summary: held_check and room_check after the swap.
checks.text: held_check, tick still held: each new piece in its planned slots at its final state, old pieces gone, every room's and cell's air as before (within 0.01 mol and 10 J plus 0.001 %). Then the tick runs until the game re-evaluates its rooms (at most 10 s) for room_check: each room beside a swap under the same id with the same cells, moles and energy within 1 % or 0.5 mol / 1 kJ; problems room_gone, room_cells_changed, room_air_changed, rooms_not_settled (the game did not run in time, such as paused). A failed swap is rolled back, so no face is left open.

include_notes.description: true: add notes, the tool's fixed text.

reference_ids.description: The walls to replace; or give room_id.

room_id.description: A room id (rooms): every wall around that room.

to.description: The new wall prefab (StructureCompositeWall); required except with job_id.

from_prefabs.description: Only pieces of these prefabs; the others are kept as not_selected.

wait.description: Queue behind a running job instead of answering busy (see jobs/queue).

confirm.description: true with dry_run false: a real run (see jobs).

from_id.description: Payer, or payers tried in order per material; default the player.

skip_unmatched.description: Leave pieces that cannot be swapped (footprint_mismatch, invalid_target) as they are instead of refusing. Default false.

refund.description: Give back what the old pieces return beyond what the new ones cost. Default true; false is refund_to none.

limit.description: Pieces listed per list in the report; default 5. All are counted and checked.

verbose.description: Confirmed run or poll: the whole job and preflight (see jobs).

For a Console or Computer Lua board, db is the computer. pins lists only the pins with a device on them.

A flight recorder: action start records a rocket every interval_s of game time; read answers a summary and one page of rows; also stop, list, clear. Recording only reads the game.

A read answers a summary (held, recorded, time span, fuel used, lowest altitude, fastest descent, peak thrust, lowest confidence and battery, the last sample, and state, target and node changes as events) plus one page of rows: offset, limit (default 12, at most 200) and every (each n-th row); has_more says more rows follow.

methods.name: rocket_forecast
methods.description:
Fly a copy of a rocket to a node, tick by tick, and report each leg: launch, hops, parking, re-entry and landing, fuel, power, thrust and the verdict. What-ifs for fuel, cargo and power. The game is not touched.
More: tool_info {tool: "rocket_forecast"}

help.text: Destination: to, else the rocket's target, else its pad. Each engine flies by its own feed law; thrust is the game's own combustion run on a copy of what each tick draws. Lines hold gas and liquid; tanks mix with their pipe by volume every tick. Plus route, uncharted, assumptions, succeeded and verdict. explain: see topic simulation.

simulation.summary: What is simulated, and what is not.
simulation.text: Physics steps and the 0.5 s game tick: gas mass, the landing autopilot, engine draws, tanks mixing, batteries paying every device's watts. Launch with gravity and the game's abort; space hops; re-entry (the confidence check once at the start, with the pad's own hop and gravity, 1 m/s2 at an Orbital Launch Mount; 0 aborts back to orbit); touchdown (soft under 2 m/s, harmless under 4, engine damage 4 to 25, faster explodes). Route: the game's pathfinder, re-planned at every node; a rocket in transit to another target turns round as the game does; a landing rocket cannot be retargeted. assumptions holds what this request and rocket change (what-ifs, stops, warnings, the first engine's thrust 100 K colder and warmer); explain adds the fixed rules: physics step, engines on, each feed law, lines keeping their make-up, power, cargo mass. Not simulated, and named with explain: heat the tanks trade with the air, boiling or condensing in the lines (the thrust 100 K colder and warmer is given), a Pressure Fed Liquid Engine's heat exchange, a mod's engine class (engine_not_modelled), the collision trigger.

legs.summary: What each leg reports, and the limits.
legs.text: Each leg: kind (launch, hop, park, landing), from, to, distance (delta-v), outcome and detail, seconds, burn_seconds, delta_v spent, fuel start, used and left mol, first tank gas kPa at the end, mass, battery, peak and recorded thrust. A landing adds confidence and band, thrusts, start altitude and mass, lowest stop altitude, touchdown speed, last rule, power_lost, fuel_ran_out. limits (default true): landing_limits, profiles (Low 25 km, Medium 40 km, High 70 km, Max 120 km) and least_fuel_mol. column_check scans the landing column above the pad.

stops.summary: A stop at a space node: park, mine, deploy, transfer, return.
stops.text: park_s: seconds at the destination. mine: miners, collectors and holds draw power; with no cargo arguments the stop fills the slots the site's yield fills in park_s. fill_holds or add_cargo_slots (1 kg each). park_load_w. deploy_payload: at a node with Deploy (the planet's orbit) the payloads leave, 20 s. transfer_mol: fuel received (negative: given). transfer_with: another rocket whose compatible gas or liquid umbilical sockets equalise by volume, as the Transfer action does. transfer_battery_j. then_return: fly back to return_to. mining: whether this loadout collects the destination's deposit, units per hour, units and slots in the stop, and problems (also warned in assumptions and the verdict).

what_ifs.text: fuel_mol, fuel_temperature_k, fuel_mix (gas and liquid names, {"LiquidHydrazine": 1}), thrust_scale (the recorded peak the landing check uses stays), throttle, cargo_slots, add_cargo_kg, payload_kg, battery_j or battery_percent, extra_load_w, profile, min_confidence (the floor for confident_mass_kg and the verdict; default 0.25).

transfer_with.description: Another rocket at the stop: compatible umbilical sockets equalise with this rocket's by volume.

transfer_battery_j.description: Battery charge received at the stop through power sockets (negative: given).

fuel_mix.description: What-if: mole fractions by gas name (Methane, Oxygen, Hydrazine...), normalised.

explain.description: Add the model's fixed rules to assumptions. Default false.

methods.description:
What a rocket can collect, by the game's own mining formulas: its loadout, and per site the yield per cycle and hour, cycles to deplete, and what stops it. Lists 3 sites. Read only.
More: tool_info {tool: "rocket_mining_options"}

help.text: sites: the node 'to' and its discovered sites, else every charted node with a deposit. collectable and not_collectable list the sites by name; collectable_only keeps the first; when it keeps nothing, notes say why (no site, nothing on board that mines, or each site's kind and the machines' reasons). explain adds to notes how Mine mode works: every miner and collector on board runs at once, and the rocket must be at the site's own node; ore and ice sites shrink every cycle, gas sites never.

loadout.text: Every Rocket Miner (on, its drill head: name, speed, ice_yield, ore_yield, health, power_factor, durability, expected_cycles_left, mines ice and ore, ice only or ore only; the miner's ore and ice speed factors; power while mining; hold_on_board), every Rocket Gas Collector (on, has_pipe_network), every Rocket Scanner (head_kind normal, surface or none, points and cycle, what it can do), cargo (holds, slots, filled, free), gas and liquid tank litres, and collects.

problems.text: An ice head at an ore site gives 0 ore while each cycle still depletes the site and wears the head. Miners skip gas sites. A collector gets something only at a gas site, and only equalises with its pipe: a pump must fill the tanks. No head, a worn head, the miner off, no cargo hold.

to.description: A node (name, map code or number, reference id): its deposit and discovered sites. Left out, every charted node with a deposit.

methods.name: rocket_status
methods.description:
Every rocket, or one, read from the game: where it is and where it goes, mass, fuel lines, engines, thrust, landing confidence, cargo, power, burn time. compact and parts shape it. Read only.
More: tool_info {tool: "rocket_status"}

help.text: explain adds explanations, once per reply: what max_recorded thrust and the landing checks mean (topics engines and landing say it too). compact leaves out mass parts, fuel tanks, power devices and checks. parts lists every part with its pose, enough to build the rocket again.
help.keys: rockets [{reference_id, network_id, name, automated_landing, auto_shut_off, manned, re_entry_profile, re_entry_altitude_m, ...}], count, explanations.

where.text: where: state (OnLaunchMount, Launching, InSpace, Landing), mode, current and target node (name, map code, code_value: the number the avionics' DestinationCode takes, charted), progress, altitude above the launch mount while launching or landing, velocity, acceleration, flight rule, and the route left as the game will fly it: re-planned at each node, fewest hops, through uncharted nodes too; a hop's distance is twice the map distance and is also its delta-v. manned: someone sits in a Crew Module Chair (only launch mounts can be targeted).

mass_fuel.text: mass: total, structure (1 kg per filled cargo slot included), gas (in the rocket's pipes, tanks and engine chambers), payload_kg, parts by kind. fuel: each engine input network (input 1 and 2 of every engine; a Pressure Fed Liquid Engine's input 2 is a heat exchanger) with pipe litres and mol, total mol, liquid mol and litres, pipe gas kPa (what pressure-fed engines read), feeds (which engine inputs draw from it), mix fractions, temperature, and its tanks (litres, mol, K, kPa, whether the game counts them for mass). pipe_networks: every pipe network on the rocket in short, engine lines and the rest such as a tanker's cargo or socket line: network_id, volume_l, total_mol, pressure_kpa, temperature_k, gases_mol, feeds (empty when no engine draws from it).

engines.text: engines: name, feed (its feed law with the game's numbers), input networks, missing_input, on, powered, throttle, thrust, mol drawn last tick, exhaust, prefab max thrust, watts, modelled. thrust: current, max_recorded, prefab_max, max_expected (what the landing check uses), achievable_full (every engine's first full-throttle tick on the lines as they are, by the game's combustion on a copy), recorded_exceeds_achievable. max_recorded: the highest thrust of all engines together on any physics step from the rocket's build on, saved with the game, reset to 0 while it has no engine. The landing check uses the larger of max_recorded and the first engine's prefab max, never the thrust the fuel gives at present; achievable_full is that. burn_time: the game's estimate, and ours at full and current throttle.

landing.text: landing_check: the confidence the Rocket Control screen shows (the ground pad's hop, world gravity). landing_at_pad: the check the game makes at re-entry toward the target pad, else its home pad: {pad, orbital (an Orbital Launch Mount uses gravity 1 m/s2), delta_v, confidence, band, min required thrust}. A landing whose check is 0 is aborted back to orbit.

other.text: collects: what the gear can bring home or do (ore, ice, gas, chart, discover, survey, surface_scan; rocket_mining_options has the detail). cargo: holds with filled, slots and kg. power: charge, capacity, percent, load per 0.5 s tick, seconds left (charge / load x 0.5), every device's watts and whether auto shut-off leaves it on. checks (self_test): the forecast's formulas against the game's numbers. parts: each hull piece and internal part with prefab, label, role, offset in metres from the engine mount in its frame, rotation as place_structure takes it, and slot contents.

methods.description:
The game's closed rooms measured cell by cell: volume, pressure, temperature, gases, heat, bounds. Every room, or the room one thing is in. Lists 10. Read only.
More: tool_info {tool: "rooms"}

help.text: A room is a closed flood fill of 2 m cells (at most 1200; a bigger or open space is outside). The air is summed fresh from each cell, as the game pools a room. Largest room first, with count and local_player_room_id. Devices come with include_devices, cell centres with include_cells.

methods.name: run_console_command
methods.description:
Cheat: run any console command and answer the lines it printed. Unrestricted and not undoable: it can spawn and delete things, teleport, start storms, change settings, quit. Ask the user first.
More: tool_info {tool: "run_console_command"}

help.text: Runs on the game's main thread. Refusals such as 'requires creative mode' and bad arguments come back as red output lines, not as a call error. On a network client some commands only queue a request to the host; run_simulation says which applies.
help.keys: command, command_key, scope, help_text, arguments, run_simulation, console_available, completes_asynchronously, output_complete, output_line_count, truncated, concurrent_log_lines, output [{time, level, text}], note.

output.summary: What the reply covers, and background commands.
output.text: Output covers only what the command printed; lines another thread logged at the same moment come as concurrent_log_lines (read_console has them too). Commands that finish on a background task (save, load, new, file, reset, log, difficulty, exportworld, upnp, steam) return before printing: completes_asynchronously is set, output_complete is false, and empty output proves nothing. Never report such a command as done from this reply; read_console a moment later and quote it. On a dedicated server the lines the server's console window would show are captured.

spawn.text: thing spawn <prefab> [amount] spawns amount FULL STACKS: 'thing spawn ItemIronIngot 1' gives one stack of the prefab's maximum, not one ingot.

refusals.text: command_not_found: no command has that name; run 'help' to list them. command_not_ready: the world is still loading, so the console would queue the command and run it later with its output lost; try again once it is loaded.

command.description: The whole command line as typed, such as 'storm start' or 'help'.

max_output_lines.description: Most lines returned; default 100. The oldest are kept: an error prints its message before its stack trace.

Watch up to 32 logic values for up to 30 s; answers their first readings and every change with its time. Read only.

Touch a control on a ScriptedScreens screen as a player's touch does: element_id, or the control at a point; click, change with value, or toggle. The script's handler runs on its next tick. Writes.

Read the screen again after the script's next tick (about 0.5 s) to see the result. Host only.

Read what a ScriptedScreens screen shows (a Console or Computer board, a tablet, a visor): its surfaces and one surface's elements with their boxes, text and props, from the host's model. image adds a PNG where the game draws. Read only.

Each element gives id, type, box {x, y, w, h} in surface pixels from the top-left (null when it needs a surface size the script did not set), shown, touch (a control screen_press can touch) and props (text, value, z_index...). methods.name: set_ic_pins
methods.description:
Set an IC Housing's pins d0 to d5 as a screwdriver does: a device id per pin, null to clear. Every pin is checked before any is written.
More: tool_info {tool: "set_ic_pins"}

help.text: Pins left out keep their device. A running chip uses the new devices from its next instruction; nothing recompiles or resets, and a multiplayer host sends the pins to clients. Returns what it altered and the pins as get_ic_status lists them. Rocket IC Housings work too; suits and other worn holders are not_ic_housing.

network.summary: Devices off the housing's data network.
network.text: On a data network, the chip reaches a pin's device only on that network, so a device off it is refused (not_on_data_network) unless allow_off_network is true; then reachable is false and the pin reads as unset until the device is cabled in. A housing with no data network reaches pinned devices anywhere.

refusals.text: device_not_found: the housing or a pin's device is outside the scope. thing_not_found: nothing has a pin's id. not_logic_device: the id is not a device (a frame, a pipe). logic_not_readable: a device with no readable logic. not_on_data_network: see network. invalid_argument: a bad pins object, pin name or id, a pin listed twice, or the housing itself. methods.name: set_ic_source
methods.description:
Write source to a circuit holder's chip, as the IC editor's export does: IC10 compiles at once and restarts at line 0; Lua compiles on a worker thread. source_file sends a large file from disk.
More: tool_info {tool: "set_ic_source"}

help.text: Give source or source_file, not both. The reply's source is null unless include_source; source_length counts what the chip stores and warnings say what storing it altered. A multiplayer host sends the chip to clients.

ic10.summary: How an IC10 source is stored and run.
ic10.text: Compiled at once and restarted at line 0; a paused chip stays paused at line 0; registers and the stack are kept (sp goes to 0). The chip stores ASCII and runs what it stores: CRLF and lone CR become LF (crlf_normalised, cr_normalised) and each non-ASCII character becomes ? (non_ascii_replaced).

editor.summary: The in-game editor's limits and the warnings for them.
editor.text: The chip runs a source of any length, but the in-game editor holds 128 lines of up to 90 characters and 4096 characters in all, and cuts a longer source when a player opens and submits it. Warnings over_editor_lines, over_editor_line_length (each long line, 0-based; past 10, their count and the first 10) and over_editor_size; the source is still written.

errors.text: compilation_error true comes with compile_error_line (0-based) and compile_error_type; error_line and error_type are the runtime error. error_line is the game's own text, a string such as "0", while compile_error_line is an integer. error_code is the game's error text without its rich-text tags.

lua.summary: How a Lua source is stored and run.
lua.text: Up to 262144 characters (larger is source_too_large), no IC10 line limits; warnings is []. StationeersLua stores it compressed, drops the old runtime and compiles the new source on a worker thread; a source that failed before is compiled again and no restart is needed. lua.compiling is usually still true in the reply: poll get_ic_status until it is false, then check lua.running and lua.last_error.

methods.name: solar_aim
methods.description:
Work out the Horizontal and Vertical (logic degrees) that point a solar panel straight at the sun, from the panel's own pivots and the sun's position. Read only: write them with write_logic.
More: tool_info {tool: "solar_aim"}

help.text: Returns reference_id, prefab_name, can_turn, operable, horizontal and vertical, off_sun_deg, alignment_ratio, sun and current. No daylight sensor and no calibration are needed. A panel without pivots (the Flat panel) reports can_turn false and a note instead of angles.

tracking.summary: Twin poses, night, and the turning tolerance.
tracking.text: Every pose (H, V) has a twin (H + 180, 180 - V) facing the cells the same way; when both reach the sun equally (within 0.1 degree) it answers the one needing the smaller turn from current, so a tracker writing every answer never swings the panel round. With the sun below the horizon the game's Ratio is 0 whatever this says; it gives the pose closest to the sun: toward where it set until midnight, toward where it will rise after. The game stops a turning panel within its rotation tolerance, up to about 0.6 degrees short in Horizontal (under 1% of Ratio).

Returns {reference_id, name, dry_run, credit_card_id, credits_before, credits_after, results, count, success_count, error_count, delivered, gas_atmosphere_id}. More: tool_info {tool: "undo_job"}

Pieces come back through place_cables, place_pipes and place_chutes (the pieces form, one run per tool and grade; a long straight as singles), so every guard applies; everything else through place_structure. paste_blueprint has its own undo.
