methods.name: vault_deposit
methods.description:
Put ingots, ores and ices straight into an Ingot Vault's store from wherever they are, with the vault's own bookkeeping; by id, in part, or by a filter over the world. Dry run by default; confirm to do it.
More: tool_info {tool: "vault_deposit"}

help.text: Each item is added to the store (an ingot's reagents times its grams; an ore's or ice's count) and destroyed, or only the part asked is taken off a stack. The vault's rule decides what it takes: ingots and ores (ices, slag and organics are ores) whose slot class fits its import slot. Host only.
help.keys: dry_run, vault {reference_id, prefab_name, display_name}, via {reference_id, prefab_name, display_name}, matched, skipped, truncated, items {results, count, success_count, error_count}, stock [{kind, prefab_name, display_name, reagent, before, change, after}].

forms.text: items [{reference_id, quantity}] (up to 256; quantity a whole count for ores, grams for ingots), reference_ids (whole items), or a filter over every item in the world: prefab_contains, name_contains, location, within_id, near_player_m, kind and limit (default 256, max 1000, nearest the player first). Items the vault does not take are left out of a filter and counted as skipped.

reply.text: {dry_run, vault, via (the Remote Vault used), matched, skipped, truncated, items {results [{index, ok, reference_id, prefab_name, display_name, kind, from {id, slot}, quantity, left_in_source}], count, success_count, error_count}, stock [{kind, prefab_name, display_name, reagent, before, change, after}]}. A real run reads after back from the vault. A refused item: thing_not_found, not_vault_material, no_reagents, in_vault_slot, slot_locked, invalid_argument (more than the stack holds, part of an ore, an item named twice).

vault_id.description: The Ingot Vault, or a Remote Vault linked to one.

reference_id.description: The item.

quantity.description: Part of the stack: a whole count of ore, grams of ingot. Default all.

items.description: Items by id, each whole or in part, up to 256.

prefab_contains.description: Filter: part of the prefab name, any case.

name_contains.description: Filter: part of the shown name, any case.

location.description: Filter: any, ground, player or stored (see items).

within_id.description: Filter: inside this holder at any depth (a backpack, a locker, a player).

near_player_m.description: Filter: within this many metres of the player.

kind.description: Filter: ingot, ore (not ice), ice, or any. Default any.

limit.description: Filter: at most this many items, nearest first; default 256.

dry_run.description: Default true: check and report only.

confirm.description: true with dry_run false to deposit.

methods.name: vault_withdraw
methods.description:
Take an amount of one stored thing out of an Ingot Vault and make it straight into a holder's slots, as the vault's own vend counts it. Dry run by default; confirm to do it.
More: tool_info {tool: "vault_withdraw"}

help.text: Name it by one of prefab_name, prefab_hash or reagent; quantity (grams of ingot, a whole count of ore) at most what the vault holds. The store goes down as a vend takes it and the same amount is made as items, never more per item than a full stack. If a game call fails part way, whatever it did not make goes back into the store. Host only.
help.keys: dry_run, vault {reference_id, prefab_name, display_name}, via {reference_id, prefab_name, display_name}, to {reference_id, prefab_name, display_name}, quantity, placed [{where, slot, quantity, reference_id}], stock [{kind, prefab_name, display_name, reagent, before, change, after}].

delivery.text: to_id is the holder (default the player); to_slot a slot index or "auto" (default). On a player, auto tops up matching stacks anywhere in the inventory, then makes new stacks in empty slots that take the item (never the body slots unless named by index); on anything else its own slots; never a hidden slot. What does not fit is no_room and nothing happens, unless allow_ground puts the rest on the ground a metre in front of the holder.

reply.text: {dry_run, vault, via, to, quantity, placed [{where (merged, slot or ground), slot {id, slot}, quantity, reference_id (null in a dry run for a new stack)}], stock [{kind, prefab_name, display_name, reagent, before, change, after}]}. A real run reads after back from the vault. Slot refusals are slot_not_found, slot_locked, slot_occupied, slot_refuses, no_slots and invalid_destination (a vault as the holder).

vault_id.description: The Ingot Vault, or a Remote Vault linked to one.

prefab_name.description: The item to take, as vault_contents names it (ItemIronIngot, ItemIronOre).

prefab_hash.description: The item to take, by prefab hash.

quantity.description: Grams of ingot, or a whole count of ore.

to_id.description: The holder that gets the items; default the player.

to_slot.description: A slot index of to_id, or "auto" (default).

allow_ground.description: Put what does not fit on the ground in front of the holder. Default false.

dry_run.description: Default true: check and report only.

confirm.description: true with dry_run false to withdraw.

methods.name: wall_map
methods.description:
A text elevation of one 2 m face plane as seen from one side, 0.5 m per character: walls, windows, doors, frames, pieces and devices; with free_rects, where a rectangle fits. Read only.
More: tool_info {tool: "wall_map"}

help.text: plane ("z=668") with around and side (default the side in a room), or looking: true (the face your look ray hits, seen from your side); radius_m default 4, max 16. Returns plane, side, right and up (the axes a column and a row step along), rows, top_left, sections, things, legend and free_rects.
help.keys: plane, side, right, up, rows, top_left {x, y, z}, sections [{face, look, reference_id, prefab_name}], things [{key, reference_id, prefab_name, display_name, position}], free_rects [{row, column, centre, cells_wide, cells_high}], legend, view {source, age_s}.

rows.text: A ruler line marks 2 m seams with |, then one line per 0.5 m, top first, left to right as seen: W wall, G window, D door, F a frame with no plate, . open, x a door's keep-out, c cable, p pipe, b both, h chute, a capital or digit a device or mounted thing over every cell its mesh box covers by more than 0.1 m. Each character covers the small cell on the plane and the one in front. A cell on a seam belongs to the section on its plus side. A passive vent or in-line tank is a thing with a key, not p.

free_rects.text: free_rects {w, h (metres, rounded up to 0.5), one_section (default true: never across a seam), require_wall (default true: only on wall, not window, frame or open), limit (default 20, max 50)} answers free_rects [{row, column (top-left on the map), centre (a world point on the plane), cells_wide, cells_high}].

plane.description: A face plane, "x=716": an axis and an even metre.

side.description: The side you view from, on the plane's axis.

looking.description: Map the face your look ray hits instead of plane.

around.description: The map's centre, [x, y, z] in metres (with plane).

radius_m.description: Half-width of the map; default 4, max 16.

one_section.description: Never across a seam. Default true.

limit.description: Rectangles returned; default 20, max 50.

free_rects.description: Find where a w by h rectangle fits (topic free_rects).

methods.name: water_sources
methods.description:
Every canister, tank, device and pipe network holding water, polluted water or steam, with location, pressure, temperature and water in moles, litres and hydration; largest first. Lists 15. Read only.
More: tool_info {tool: "water_sources"}

help.text: Room and world air, bodies, organs, bottles and packets (consumables lists those) are left out. Sources under min_mol (default 1 mol, 0.018 L) are skipped. Water is drunk through a water bottle filler or a drinking fountain on a pipe network; polluted water needs a water purifier first and steam must condense. owner.kind is item, structure, dynamic (a portable tank) or pipe_network.
help.keys: sources [{kind, owner, atmosphere_id, volume_l, pressure_kpa, temperature_k, water}], count, totals {liquid_mol, liquid_l, hydration, polluted_mol, polluted_l, ...}, min_mol, local_player {reference_id, display_name, position}.

timing.text: A pipe network is listed from the moment it exists, even while paused; a thing's own atmosphere made after the last atmospherics tick (a canister spawned while paused) is listed from the next tick on.

min_mol.description: Skip sources holding less water, polluted water and steam together; default 1 mol.

min_moles.description: Old name of min_mol, still read; min_mol wins.

methods.name: weather
methods.description:
The storm schedule, the world's weather events and the season: what is coming, when, and when the next event can schedule. Read only.
More: tool_info {tool: "weather"}

help.text: Returns world_has_weather, state (None, StormScheduled, Storm, RainScheduled, Rain, SnowScheduled, Snow), current, days_past, days_since_last, cooldown_days, world_start_delay_days, can_schedule_now, schedulable_in_days, events and season.

schedule.summary: How the game schedules an event.
schedule.text: current: null, or {id, name, running, starts_in_s (negative once running), length_s, ends_in_s}. An event can schedule once days_since_last > cooldown_days and days_past > world_start_delay_days (7 times the difficulty's starting weather multiplier); schedulable_in_days counts the whole days until both pass. The game then picks an event at random and draws its start delay and length, so starts_in_s is exact from that moment. While an event is current nothing new schedules; when it ends days_since_last goes to 0 and a new cooldown is drawn.

events.summary: The events a world can roll, and the season.
events.text: events [{id, name, cooldown_days_min, cooldown_days_max (the largest the game can draw), start_delay_s_min, start_delay_s_max, duration_s_min, duration_s_max, temperature_offset_day_k, temperature_offset_night_k, solar_ratio, active_in_orbit}]. season: null before the orbit loads, else {true_anomaly_deg (0 at perihelion), year_length_days, solar_energy_percent, day_of_year}. Terraforming Reloaded can stop a stripped world scheduling storms by its own setting; this tool does not model that.

methods.name: write_logic
methods.description:
Write one logic value to a device, by logic type name or number, as a chip or console would. Answers the value read back at once.
More: tool_info {tool: "write_logic"}

help.text: Returns requested_value, previous_value and current_value. current_value is read back at once and can differ from the request: the device clamps it (On 7 reads 1), ignores it (a colour index only paint sets), or moves toward it over time (a solar panel turning). The write still succeeds.

gateway_id.description: Omit or 'world' for every device; a gateway id narrows to its data networks (see gateways).

reference_id.description: The device's reference id (list_devices).

logic_type.description: A logic type name (Temperature) or number.

value.description: The value to write: a finite number.

methods.name: write_logic_many
methods.description:
Write up to 256 logic values in order in one call; each result stands alone, by index, with its own error.
More: tool_info {tool: "write_logic_many"}

help.text: Each result is {index, ok, reference_id, logic_type, requested_value, previous_value, current_value} (current_value read back as write_logic does), or {index, ok: false, reference_id, logic_type, error}; reference_id and logic_type are null when the entry's own could not be read.
help.keys: gateway_id, results, count, success_count, error_count.

gateway_id.description: Omit or 'world' for every device; a gateway id narrows to its data networks (see gateways).

reference_id.description: The device's reference id (list_devices).

logic_type.description: A logic type name (Temperature) or number.

value.description: The value to write: a finite number.

writes.description: The writes, up to 256, each {reference_id, logic_type, value}, applied in order.

methods.name: write_memory
methods.description:
Cheat: write up to 512 values into a device's memory from start_address, as a chip's put does. Ask the user first. Nothing is written when the range runs past the last address.
More: tool_info {tool: "write_memory"}

help.text: Writes the memory read_memory reads; a Logic Memory has none (memory_not_writable). A range past the memory's last address is invalid_argument and nothing is written. An IC Housing or suit without a chip is no_programmable_chip.

gateway_id.description: Omit or 'world' for every device; a gateway id narrows to its data networks (see gateways).

reference_id.description: The device's reference id (list_devices).

start_address.description: The first address to write, from 0.

values.description: The values, finite numbers, 1 to 512, written from start_address on.
